title: 37 'real' North Staffordshire ghost sightings to terrify you this Halloween
excerpt: These ghost sightings will send a shiver down your spine
content:
These ghost sightings will send a shiver down your spine

16:37, 31 Oct 2026

Most people have seen something inexplicable. But there are far less people who believe they've seen something of the paranormal.

‌

‌

And if you've seen it, would you still really believe it? Stoke-on-Trent has a long history, and some tales are still told as the winter draws in, and the nights grow endless and dark.

‌

It's easy to dismiss in the cold light of day. But there is one man who has spent a fair chunk of his life documenting every creepy story across the UK including dozens in this area. Dr Paul Lee - a famous paranormal researcher - has dedicated nearly a decade to tracking ghostly goings on.

‌

Among those on our doorstep include the fire-hit Leopard Hotel in Burslem, where supposedly the statue of a horse was thrown across the bar, and children were heard singing 'Ring-o-ring-o-roses'.

In Apedale Heritage Centre, the miners who died working there seem to have never really left. In the end, Dr Lee compiled 5,592 locations that he believes are haunted - and these include 37 spots in our creepy neck of the wood.

Here are all the spooky happenings from around Stoke-on-Trent and North Staffordshire

Paralysis Escape Rooms, Hanley

‌

According to press reports, some of the claimed phenomena include, "a woman humming the tune to 10 Green Bottles, a little girl giggling, and a stern male spectre telling her to 'sh'." CCTV caught the lid of a glass decanter falling off and landing on the floor of the manager's office. There have also been stories of hair being messed with and clothing being pulled.

Regent Theatre, Hanley

‌

Two old ladies, from the 1950s era, have been seen walking towards the theatre but vanish before reaching it. Loud bangs and other sounds, cold spots and a spectral lady who sits in on shows but disappears halfway through have been reported inside. Other reports mention a "lonely looking man" staring out from a balcony, a young girl in the auditorium, and figures rushing through the corridors.

The Potteries Museum and Art Gallery, Hanley

‌

People have observed items moving by themselves and the canopy of a Spitfire aircraft has been found opened, the smell of fumes and smoke has been detected - unusually, this aircraft never saw active duty.

Victoria Hall, Hanley

‌

People have been observed sitting in the auditorium as if waiting for a performance - but they shortly afterwards disappear. Music has also been heard coming from the empty orchestra pit too.

Etruria Hall, Etruria

‌

The home of Josiah Wedgwood and now a wedding and meetings venue for the nearby Best Western Hotel, there have been stories of unexplained banging and clanking noises during renovation work.

Etruria Industrial Museum

‌

A ghostly barge, sighted in 1998, and the sound of a woman crying have been reported here.

King's Hall, Stoke

‌

Music "from decades ago" and a young boy who vanishes after asking for help have been encountered here.

Royal Stoke University Hospital

‌

The nursing staff have talked of being accompanied by another, unexplained nurse described as like an elderly matron with a well-spoken English accent, but rarely seen by patients. One nurse described how she saw a girl of 4 years old, wearing a red coat. Objects have also been moved and the sound of starched, rustling clothing has been heard.

Newcastle Players Workshop

‌

The spectre could be Colin Minton Campbell, who funded this institute, in the 1960s the phantom was seen to glide from the balcony area into the building next door.

The Leopard, Burslem

‌

A number of phenomena have been reported here, the statue of a horse being flung across the bar, the bell for last orders ringing by itself, glasses being thrown, doors slamming, shadowy figures and even the sound of children singing "Ring-o-ring-o-roses." Candles that had been lit in the disused hotel rooms have also been found extinguished, and a reporter who visited found that the door had seemingly locked itself.

St John the Baptist Church, Burslem

‌

High pitched voices, whistles and a lady sometimes visits the grave of Molly Leigh before vanishing Molly's pet blackbird has reportedly been seen in the churchyard, Molly was not a well liked member of the community and appeared to a Reverend who visited her home, with the intention of helping himself to her belongings Afterwards, her coffin was re-opened and an exorcism performed after which the poor bird was sealed inside.

Ford Green Hall, Smallthorne

‌

Spectral occurrences were so common here that one curator became used to them on a daily basis - during one tour a visitor ended up chatting to a figure, not knowing that it was a ghost, or that she was the only one who could see the phantom. In recent years, footsteps have been heard in what used to be a corridor in the hall chamber, and a long haired black and brown tabby cat ran under the feet of a worker as he was carrying boxes - but a search revealed no trace of the animal.

Queen's Park, Longton

‌

A number of phantoms have been reported here, including: an angry man in "fine clothes" and a top hat by the clock tower, a little boy on the old train line, a jogger in a tree (!) and the lady of the lake.

Gladstone Pottery Museum, Longton

‌

The sound of someone running and bangs have been heard, and strange smells detected on the stairs that lead up to the gallery, additionally, objects are said to be thrown, move by themselves or be re-arranged, and doors have been flung open. With regards to visible phantoms, an old man with "a fine set of whiskers" and wearing a smock, has been mentioned, as have cloth-capped children playing "ring-a-ring-o' roses" in the courtyard, a phantom lady in Victorian clothing who exudes the scent of lavender as she walks by people, and "a burly, bare-knuckle fighter near one of the kilns who is said to shout at anyone who goes near the area he haunts.

Short Street, Longton

‌

Cigarette smoke has been detected here, as have voices, and a ghostly cat has been seen sitting in front of the cottages.

Trentham Gardens

‌

A spectral horse and rider, marching soldiers and phantom nuns have been reported here.

Trentham Hall

‌

A "Grey Lady" walks in the Italian Garden, believed to be a servant, also a man who walks a dog on a lead, and music with no obvious origin have been experienced here.

Harecastle Tunnel, Kidsgrove

‌

A "Boggart" is said to haunt this tunnel and that she can be heard crying, others report a female ghost without a head, the local story being that her husband decapitated her after finding out that she was having an affair.

The Victoria, May Bank

‌

The resident ghost at this pub is called "Percy" according to the Ember Inns website. There is no more information other than he is supposed to be very friendly!

Apedale Heritage Centre

‌

The ghost of miners who died working here are said to haunt the tunnels.

Keele Hall

‌

The male phantom here is believed to be that of Michael, the Grand Duke of Russia. Another spectre is that of maid who seems to be inspecting a long-gone doorway.

Whitmore Hall

‌

The ghost of a young stable boy has been encountered and his screams heard in the stable block, where he perished in a fire. Inside the main house, spectral music played on a clavichord has been heard.

Beech Caves

‌

There are reports of "shadow people", cloaked figures and strange voices here.

Eccleshall Castle

‌

A "Grey Lady" has been seen here, sometimes described as being sad and wearing a bridal dress and intriguingly, a wall behind her. There are also reports of a "White Lady", a Cavalier and a large black dog which is sometimes seen at dusk.

Broughton Hall, Eccleshall (the home of billionaire John Caudwell)

‌

A phantom known as "Red Socks" or "Red Stockings" haunts this building - a cleaning lady felt someone near her as she cleaned the long gallery attic and staircase. She saw a man walking down the staircase, described as solid with red socks, and she stood up to greet him, but the man walked through her, there are also tales of something invisible brushing past people on these stairs. The legend is that a young heir to the Broughton family saw Cromwell's forces marching up the drive and yelled his allegiance to the king from a window, whereupon the troops opened fire at him. The young man staggered down the stairs, blood pouring everywhere, including his socks and he died shortly afterwards. It is not clear if this phantom recurs or if this sighting was a "one off." Another version of the tale says that he was hit in the Long Gallery, but managed to crawl to one of the bedrooms where he perished. Several women have slept in this bed and felt it vibrate.

Charnes Hall, Eccleshall

‌

A beautiful young lady in a "billowing white gown" or shroud has been seen here, apparently looking for a wedding ring that was stolen from her finger by a servant after she was laid out in a coffin. Another version of the story is that it was a man who took her ring, chopping off her finger in the process which awoke the lady as she had wrongly been thought to have died, she lived for many years afterwards. Because of her clothing, she is nicknamed "Silky.

St Mary's and All Saints Church, Checkley

‌

A spectral monk, thought to be the last abbot of Croxden Thomas Chawney, has been seen at night in the graveyard. A phantom white dog has also been reported, and one witness saw it run through a wall.

The Old Rectory, Checkley

‌

The widow of Reverend William Hutchinson, haunts this building, where she is said to give disapproving looks at people It is not clear if she is still seen here, though.

St Lawrence's Church, Rushton Spencer

‌

The ghost of Tom Meaykin has been seen in the churchyard here, the daughter of a local apothecary fell in love with him but her father disapproved as Tom was a mere servant One day Tom dropped dead but sightings of his spectre caused townsfolk to exhume the body where they discovered that he had buried alive and local gossip blamed the apothecary for administering a suitable drug Tom was reburied in his home town of Rushton Spencer.

Lud's Church, Gradbach

‌

This ravine was once the make-shift church in the 15th century for John Wyclif and his followers, the Lollards. However, the group was under threat of persecution, and a group of soldiers unearthed their den, ordering the Lollards to surrender. The congregation reached for their swords and one of the soldiers reacted instinctively, firing an arrow that killed Alice, the granddaughter of Lollard leader Walter de Lud Auk. The group buried the young child at the entrance to the ravine and then surrendered, it is said that her spirit is still seen where her remains were interred.

Westwood College, Leek

‌

The ghost of a lady has been seen draped over a gate in the grounds of the college. It is said that the phantom is Lady Tempest Vale, who was killed when she spurred her horse to jump over a double gate.

The Green Dragon, Leek (Wetherspoons)

‌

Formerly known as "The Swan", some say that Tolkien, who used this building during his writing projects, visits his former haunt Another spectre pinches barmaids or blows on their hair, but one lady was hit on the head by a flying bottle - which could not be found afterwards Doors have also been known to close behind people, and sometimes would seem to be locked - but was found to be open when staff came to rescue the trapped visitor.

Alton Towers

‌

In the house itself, the ghost of the "Black Lady" has been seen, and the smell of lavendar and roses detected. A black dog, a hunchback and voices have also been detected. A large man in black has been seen in the area of the music room, where footsteps have been heard. A shadowy figure and more footfalls have been experienced in the banqueting hall. The ladies toilets have played host to a spectre, who is described as unhappy and wears a black cloak, hat and boots. There are also stories of stones being thrown by something invisible. In the vicinity of the ride called "The Hex" are stories of a man in black, and a spectre in riding clothes. There are also tales of phantom soldiers, but details are lacking.

Hilderstone Hall

‌

Now a care home for the elderly, various strange sounds have been heard here including furniture moving, footsteps, a clock being wound and doors opening and closing.

Blake Mere Pond, Thorncliffe

‌

It is said that a mermaid was rescued from confinement by a sailor and released into the lake. He visited the mermaid every day but when he died, the mermaid became resentful and in death haunted the lake, where she would harm any visitors. A second legend is that the ghost is that of a young woman who was drowned here after she rejected a man named Joshua Linnet. In revenge, he accused her of being a witch and the townsfolk executed her. She vowed vengance on Joshua and his body was found three days later in the lake. The lady is still said to haunt the area.

The Greyhound Inn, Warslow

‌

A newspaper clipping from 1993 states that a young serving maid from the 18th century has been seen here, sitting quietly next to the fire late at night

St Leonard's Churchyard, Ipstones

‌

A disembodied voices that whispers a foreign language in people's ears has been heard here, and at Horseley's Stone, a spirit of a little bird is said to appear which is meant to be an omen of good luck.
